tagline: Build one batch pipeline from raw extracts to a tested, governed open table that two engines read
description: Participants build one batch pipeline end to end for Qafila, the fictional trading company of the Academy's data engineering course, whose margin report nobody trusts. They query raw extracts with analytical SQL, ingest an API and a database change feed incrementally, clean with dataframes, model a star schema with a slowly changing supplier dimension, write tested transformations and a data contract, orchestrate them, and land the result in an open table format that a second engine reads. Day four adds distributed processing, streaming and governance.
audience: Practitioners: engineers and analysts who already write SQL and work with Python dataframes, and who now need a batch pipeline that is incremental, tested, held by a contract and governed.
prerequisites: FN-102 Command Line, Git and Reproducible Projects
Writes SQL joins, grouping and simple window functions
Filters and joins tables with a Python dataframe library
Commits with Git from a shell
Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. No model, no key, no Docker, no cloud account. Run 00_setup_check before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Analyse raw transactional extracts with analytical SQL, including window functions and incremental predicates, given three months of synthetic orders, shipments and prices in columnar files
outcomes.evidence: queries that reproduce the reference monthly margin and a note on two defects found

outcomes.text: Implement incremental ingestion from an API and a change feed, keeping supplier history as a slowly changing dimension, given a paginated API and a feed with updates and deletes
outcomes.evidence: loads that add no duplicates on re-run and correct validity ranges

outcomes.text: Design a dimensional model at a stated grain and build it as tested, version-controlled transformations, given the finance team's five margin questions
outcomes.evidence: a star schema, passing tests and a rebuild that skips unchanged models

outcomes.text: Build an orchestrated pipeline with a data contract, quality gates, retries and backfills that fails safely when an upstream feed breaks, given a supplier feed that changes its schema without notice
outcomes.evidence: a run log showing the violation caught, the mart left unrefreshed and a backfill after the fix

outcomes.text: Configure an open table format with partitioning, schema evolution and time travel, and read it from a second engine, given the margin mart and one schema change
outcomes.evidence: identical results from two engines and a query against an earlier snapshot

outcomes.text: Classify every field under the national classification levels and apply minimisation, masking and access rules, given the customer and supplier tables
outcomes.evidence: a classification register and a masked view that passes access tests

case_study.name: Qafila Trading
case_study.summary: Qafila Trading is a fictional importer and wholesaler of food and household goods in Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam, selling to 240 shops, restaurants and hotels and buying from 18 suppliers in five countries. Its finance controller, Lujain Al-Zamil, does not trust the monthly margin report. Participants rebuild it as one pipeline: order extracts, a paginated supplier price API, a supplier change feed and a shipment event stream, all synthetic, generated with a fixed seed and planted with the problems the labs find.

days.title: Capstone: the margin mart and its defence

capstone.summary: The margin mart from raw sources to an Apache Iceberg table, built on the course's Qafila capstone starter (labs/capstone/): incremental ingestion of the supplier API and the change feed with supplier history, a star schema at order-line grain, tested transformations and a data contract, an orchestrated run that blocks on a broken feed and backfills after the fix, and classification and masking of customer and supplier fields.
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository link. The assessor re-runs the pipeline from a clean checkout; the README reports row counts, test results and run times, and the commit history and run logs are in the repository. Then an eight-minute defence of one modelling decision, in which the participant also explains one transformation the assessor selects.
